question: Why did international volleyball stop letting only the serving team score?
answer: To make matches fit a schedule. Under side-out scoring a long run of rallies could pass with no point at all, so nobody could say how long a match would last. In 1999 the international federation switched to rally scoring, a point on every rally, and match lengths became predictable enough to sell to television.
move: When something must fit a schedule, expect its rules to bend to the clock.
source: LSU Athletics, a point on every play
